name: ci-ccache-linux
title: CI: ccache on the three Linux legs (cache saved only from master pushes)
issue: Analysis and decisions: C:/Method Notes Obsidian/orchestrator/proposals/ci-speedup.md (read it fully first: measured per-leg times, critical path, the queueing finding, risks). The user APPROVED (2026-10-15): (1) the cheap workflow-only change below; (2) Linux ccache AFTER that, then decide on Windows after measuring; (3) ALL 8 legs stay on every PR (do NOT remove or move any leg, do NOT rename any job: the required check is `linux (Release, x86_64, Clang)`, the other jobs are `linux (Release, x86_64, GCC 14)`, `linux (Release, arm64, Clang)`, `windows (Debug, PhysX ON)`, `windows (Release, PhysX ON)`, `windows (Debug, PhysX OFF, FreeType ON, ufbx ON, TLS ON)`, `docker (editor host image, x86_64)`, `protocol (generated clients, golden vectors)`). Constraints: workflow-only changes (.github/workflows/), no source changes; nothing can be tested locally: the PR's own CI run is the test, so write the YAML defensively, re-read it for syntax/indentation, and prefer GitHub's documented semantics (verify them in your head against docs you know: concurrency groups, job-level `if`, `needs`, skipped-job handling for required checks (a job skipped by a job-level `if` reports 'skipped' and a skipped required check counts as passing; a skipped job whose `needs` failed does NOT), `fromJSON`, cache action rules (caches created on a PR ref are not readable by sibling PRs; the default branch cache is readable by PRs)). The orchestrator's own tooling polls check-runs by head sha and treats conclusions `failure|cancelled|timed_out` as failed and counts `completed` runs: a superseded run that gets cancelled is expected; a skipped job is fine; do not rely on anything else. Do NOT touch the merge gates or ratify tooling. SCOPE: edit .github/workflows/tests.yml (the three Linux jobs: x86_64 Clang (required), arm64 Clang, x86_64 GCC 14; leave Windows and docker alone) and docs/testing.html. Read the current Linux jobs first (apt dependencies, the CMake configure lines, how the build is invoked (ninja? cmake --build), the lavapipe/Vulkan steps added by the Vulkan work). Add ccache: install it with apt (add `ccache` to the apt line), configure CMake with `-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER=ccache` for these legs only, set CCACHE_DIR/CCACHE_MAXSIZE (e.g. 1G per leg; sloppiness minimal: `CCACHE_COMPILERCHECK=content`, `CCACHE_BASEDIR=${{ github.workspace }}`, `CCACHE_NOHASHDIR=true` so different checkout paths do not matter), restore/save the ccache directory with actions/cache keyed per leg + compiler + a rotating suffix (key like `ccache-<leg>-<github.run_id>`, restore-keys `ccache-<leg>-`), where the SAVE happens ONLY on pushes to master (e.g. use actions/cache/restore on PRs and actions/cache/save guarded by `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/master'` with `if: always()` caveats thought through) so PR runs read the default-branch cache but never pollute it; print `ccache -s` (hit rate, size) at the end of each leg into the job summary ($GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY) so cold vs warm results are measurable; make sure the clang-20 from apt.llvm.org leg and the GCC leg each get their OWN cache (different compilers must not share), that PhysX/FetchContent downloads are unaffected, and that a cache miss/failure never fails the build (continue-on-error on the cache steps). Think through: ccache and precompiled headers (none today), `-fdebug-prefix-map` not needed with NOHASHDIR, the Vulkan SPIR-V shader compile step (glslangValidator custom commands are not cached by ccache: fine), `-fprofile`/coverage flags (none). Docs: a paragraph in docs/testing.html CI section (what is cached, how to read `ccache -s`, that only master saves). Unverified items to list: the real warm-cache speed-up (the FIRST run is cold; measure on the NEXT PR after this one has merged and master has saved a cache), hit rates, and cache size limits (GitHub's per-repo cache quota is 10 GB: report the expected total). The PR's own CI run must stay green on all 8 checks. CONTEXT UPDATE: PR #150 (cancel superseded runs + docs-only skip) is MERGED: tests.yml now has a `changes (docs-only check)` job, concurrency cancel-in-progress for pull_request events, job-level `if: needs.changes.outputs.docs_only != 'true'` on the Linux and docker jobs and step-level skips in the Windows matrix job: re-read the CURRENT tests.yml on master first and integrate the ccache steps into that structure (the Linux jobs now `needs: changes`; keep job names, the `if` and `needs` untouched; ccache steps must also respect the docs-only skip: they live inside the skipped jobs so they skip with them). Because concurrency cancels older PR runs, make sure a cancelled run cannot save a partial cache (saves happen only on master pushes, which are never cancelled).
acceptance: All 8 checks green with unchanged names; the 3 Linux legs build through ccache with per-leg caches
Caches are saved only from master pushes and only read on PRs; ccache -s printed to the job summary
A cache restore/save failure never fails a job
notes: Reviewer: check cache key/restore-keys logic and that PR runs cannot save into the shared cache, compiler/launcher flags only on the three Linux legs, apt line, env var scoping, summary step runs even on failure, nothing else in the jobs changed. Unverified: warm-run savings (measured after the first master run).
